key_insight: Adversarial training can be added after pretraining to improve pixel diffusion models, helping them capture fine-scale natural image details more faithfully. The paper shows that this correction works without changing the core model architecture or replacing the original diffusion objective.
problem_solved: Pixel diffusion models generate images directly in RGB space, but they still miss or weaken subtle natural-image statistics such as fine textures and local realism. This paper addresses the quality gap between visually good samples and truly realistic fine-grained image detail.
method: Start from a pretrained pixel diffusion or flow-matching model.
Keep the original generative objective unchanged, and add an adversarial loss on predicted outputs at non-high-noise timesteps.
Use adversarial learning as a post-training correction to improve realism and fine-detail fidelity without redesigning the model.
impact: This gives practitioners a practical way to boost image quality in pixel-space generative models without the complexity of adding an autoencoder pipeline. It is especially useful when the goal is sharper, more natural-looking images with better local statistics.
